guards.what: FOUR-VERB COVERAGE (enchant / upgrade+downgrade / transform / copy) -- stated explicitly so the hole cannot reopen silently. Verb 3, TRANSFORM: CardCmd.Transform (CardCmd.cs:369-451) removes the original from its pile and adds a freshly-built replacement; it never touches Enchantment, and the destroyed original takes its enchantment with it
guards.maps_to: TRANSFORM verdict: FAITHFUL, both engines drop the enchantment. C#: CardCmd.Transform's loop takes `item.GetReplacement(rng)`, calls `item.Original.RemoveFromCurrentPile()` (CardCmd.cs:400) and adds the replacement (CardCmd.cs:437/440); the word Enchantment does not appear anywhere in the method, and neither AfterTransformedFrom nor AfterTransformedTo (CardModel.cs:1625-1631, both empty virtuals -- SovereignBlade is the only override in the source) moves it. So the enchantment dies with the original. SIM: run.transform_card (run.py:406-470) and CardCmd.transform_to_random (cmds.py:415-449) both build the replacement with `make_card(...)`, which carries no enchantment. EXECUTED, this unit: `py -c "import sys,random;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from sts2_rl.run import RunState;from sts2_rl.cards import make_card;from sts2_rl.enchantments import make_enchantment;r=RunState(rng=random.Random(0));c=make_card('strike');r.deck=[c];e=make_enchantment('corrupted');e.amount=2;e.attach(c);n=r.transform_card(c,into=make_card('bash'));print(n.id, n.enchantment)"` -> `bash None`, matching C#. The in-combat twin (CardCmd.transform_to_random on a Sharp'd Strike) also prints a replacement with `enchantment=None`. Same result for all 17 ids. COVERAGE TABLE for this unit -- (1) ENCHANT: the CanEnchantCardType hook entry plus the reachability guard above. (2) UPGRADE / DOWNGRADE: cannot bite here, and that is now executed rather than assumed: `py -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from sts2_rl.enchantments import ALL_ENCHANTMENTS, Enchantment;print(sorted(k for k,v in ALL_ENCHANTMENTS.items() if v.attach is not Enchantment.attach))"` -> `['goopy','souls','steady','tezcataras_ember']`. Only those four override attach() to mutate a static card property (exhausts / retain / cost / eternal), so only those four can be undone by the card rebuild that upgrade()/downgrade() performs. This unit is not one of them -- it works through the modify_* hooks, which are read live off the still-attached enchantment -- so upgrade and downgrade are no-ops for it. (3) TRANSFORM: this entry, faithful. (4) COPY: guard EG2, gap. All four verbs are now on the record; before this pass transform and copy were 0/17.

guards.what: EG2: card COPY drops the enchantment. C# CardModel.CreateClone (CardModel.cs:2168) -> MutableClone -> DeepCloneFields re-attaches the source card's enchantment onto the copy -- CardModel.cs:1204-1209 `(EnchantmentModel)Enchantment.ClonePreservingMutability()`, `Enchantment = null`, `EnchantInternal(clone, clone.Amount)` -- and does the same for the Affliction two lines down (1210-1215). CreateClone itself throws unless the card sits in a COMBAT pile (CardModel.cs:2170-2173), so every copy site is a combat-pile copy. The sim's copy sites rebuild the card from its class and carry only the upgrade level.
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-28: all five rebuild copy sites now route through `create_clone` (cards/base.py:57-83), which rebuilds the card AND re-attaches a `clone_preserving_mutability()` copy of the source's enchantment (enchantments.py:109-117 + attach at :119-125) and a copy of its affliction -- the port of CardModel.DeepCloneFields (CardModel.cs:1204-1215). The five: cards/trash_heap_cards.py:20-24 `_clone` (Dual Wield), powers.py:883-893 (JugglingPower), relics/music_box.py:44-49, cards/anger.py:36-38 and relics/burning_sticks.py:33-37. WAS: each was a bare `type(card)()` rebuild carrying only the upgrade level, so the copy lost the enchantment entirely. The false `_clone` docstring is fixed too (trash_heap_cards.py:20-23 now says it carries the enchantment and the affliction, and it does). The enchantment now RIDES ALONG on the copy and every DIRECT-CALL leg works (DamageCmd/BlockCmd read `card.enchantment` straight off the card, cmds.py:115-118 and :219-222; `attach` re-runs modify_card so static keywords/cost are on the copy). What REMAINS is that the copy's enchantment is never made a LISTENER: CardPileCmd._enter_combat (cmds.py:569-576) registers only the card, not `card.enchantment`, and never sets `enchantment.combat`. C# has no such step -- CombatState.IterateHookListeners re-enumerates from the piles on every dispatch and adds `cardModel.Enchantment` (CombatState.cs:449-467, the add at :462-465) -- so the game's copy is a full listener. RESIDUAL FOR THIS UNIT, and it is now a CRASH rather than a silent divergence: Corrupted's self-damage leg is `on_play`, which reaches the engine through `self.combat.hooks` (enchantments.py:517-527), and the copy's enchantment has `combat = None`. EXECUTED 2026-07-28: build a combat, `create_clone` a Corrupted Strike, add it to hand and play it -> `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'hooks'`. The 1.5x multiplier leg DOES now work on the copy (direct call). LIVE.
